main.title: Professor Layton and the Azran Legacy
main.subtitle: An ancient mystery takes to the air
main.summary: Professor Layton and the Azran Legacy is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS puzzle adventure concluding the series' prequel trilogy. Layton, Luke and Emmy join the archaeologist Desmond Sycamore after a discovery involving a girl preserved in ice. Their investigation leads toward the vanished Azran civilisation and a journey aboard the airship Bostonius. The premise expands the professor's travels beyond a single town. Different destinations become parts of one archaeological question, with the familiar habit of stopping to solve a puzzle accompanying a much wider expedition.

cards.heading: An ancient mystery takes to the air
cards.text: Professor Layton and the Azran Legacy is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS puzzle adventure concluding the series' prequel trilogy. Layton, Luke and Emmy join the archaeologist Desmond Sycamore after a discovery involving a girl preserved in ice. Their investigation leads toward the vanished Azran civilisation and a journey aboard the airship Bostonius. The premise expands the professor's travels beyond a single town. Different destinations become parts of one archaeological question, with the familiar habit of stopping to solve a puzzle accompanying a much wider expedition.

cards.heading: Five discoveries across the world
cards.text: The search for five Azran eggs sends the group to a selection of distant locations. Players investigate their inhabitants and surroundings using the touchscreen magnifying glass, revealing conversations, hint coins and puzzles. These separate destinations give each local mystery a place within the expedition's larger purpose. Travelling aboard the Bostonius connects them, allowing the adventure to move between distinct settings instead of keeping every discovery inside one enclosed community. The recurring tools remain easy to recognise even when the scenery and the immediate problem change.

cards.heading: The last part of an earlier journey
cards.text: The story brings together questions raised by the prequel adventures while continuing to make individual puzzles the player's regular contribution. A character may need help, an object may conceal another clue or an apparently simple task may require a different reading. The expedition provides a reason for these encounters to accumulate across a larger map. As the final prequel chapter, Azran Legacy gives Layton's earlier travels a destination, keeping Luke and Emmy alongside him while the discoveries connect personal relationships with the remains of a much older world.

main.title: SimCity
main.subtitle: Connected cities and the consequences of an online launch
main.summary: Maxis rebuilds SimCity around the GlassBox simulation and cities that share resources. Its mandatory internet connection becomes central to both the design and the troubled March 2013 launch.

cards.heading: GlassBox rebuilds the city simulation
cards.text:
SimCity is a city-building and urban planning simulation massively multiplayer online game developed by Maxis Emeryville and published by Electronic Arts. Released for Microsoft Windows in early March 2013, it is a reboot of the SimCity series, and is the first major installment since the release of SimCity 4 a decade before. A macOS version was released on August 29, 2013.

Players can create a settlement that can grow into a city by zoning land for residential, commercial, or industrial development, as well as building and maintaining public services, transport and utilities. SimCity uses a new engine called GlassBox that allows for more detailed simulation than previous games. Throughout its development, SimCity received critical acclaim for its new engine and reimagined gameplay; publications cautioned the game's mandatory use of a persistent internet connection, however, which enables cloud saves and multiplayer functionality, allowing cities to trade and share resources.

cards.heading: Regions share services while data layers explain the city
cards.text: A city's decisions travel beyond its borders. Traffic and pollution follow regional connections, while neighbouring cities can exchange resources or share services such as health care and rubbish collection. Their combined wealth can fund a major project, including an airport or solar power plant. Within the city, information views make these relationships easier to inspect. Selecting water reveals its underground distribution; the sewage view shows where capacity is failing. Colour and animation turn services that would otherwise remain abstract into visible flows, giving the player specific places to improve rather than only a balance sheet.

cards.heading: Mandatory connectivity overwhelms the launch
cards.text: Prior to release, SimCity received positive reviews; nonetheless, the game's launch was received negatively due to widespread technical and gameplay problems related to the mandatory network connection for playing and saving game data. These issues included network outages, problems with saving progress and difficulty connecting to the game's servers. As a result, reviewers were unable to review the game, labeling the launch a "disaster" and the game "unplayably broken", urging players to avoid purchasing the game until the issues were resolved. SimCity was the last game by Maxis Emeryville before the studio's closure in 2015.

main.title: Tomb Raider
main.subtitle: Lara Croft begins again on Yamatai
main.summary: Tomb Raider is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Crystal Dynamics and published by Square Enix.

cards.heading: A new beginning for Lara Croft
cards.text: Tomb Raider is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Crystal Dynamics and published by Square Enix. It is the tenth main entry and a reboot of the Tomb Raider series, acting as the first instalment in the Survivor trilogy that reconstructs the origins of Lara Croft. The game was released for PlayStation 3, Windows, and Xbox 360 on 5 March 2013. Gameplay focuses on survival, with exploration when traversing the island and visiting various optional tombs. It is the first game in the main series to have multiplayer and the first game in the series to be published by Square Enix after the latter's acquisition of Eidos Interactive in 2009.

cards.heading: Yamatai and Camilla Luddington as Lara
cards.text: Crystal Dynamics began development of Tomb Raider soon after the release of Tomb Raider: Underworld in 2008. Rather than a sequel, the team decided to reboot the series, re-establishing the origins of Lara Croft for the second time, as they did with Tomb Raider: Legend. Tomb Raider is set on Yamatai, an island from which Lara, who is untested and not yet the battle-hardened explorer she is in other titles in the series, must save her friends and escape while being hunted down by a malevolent cult. Camilla Luddington was hired to voice and perform as Lara Croft, replacing Keeley Hawes.

cards.heading: Acclaim and later editions
cards.text: Critics praised the graphics, Camilla Luddington's performance and Lara's development, while questioning the multiplayer addition. Sales exceeded 14.5 million by October 2021. The Definitive Edition first reached PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in 2014, and the story continued through Rise of the Tomb Raider and Shadow of the Tomb Raider.

main.title: Soul Sacrifice
main.subtitle: A prisoner reads a way to survive
main.summary: Soul Sacrifice is Marvelous AQL and Japan Studio's PlayStation Vita action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 7 March 2013. A prisoner awaiting sacrifice encounters Librom, a talking book containing the memories of a sorcerer's battles. Entering its stories lets the prisoner gain the experience needed to challenge Magusar, the captor waiting outside. Each mission becomes another remembered encounter with a monster, connecting repeated battles to the account inside the book. The bleak setting makes the power offered to the player feel dangerous before its cost is fully understood.

cards.heading: A prisoner reads a way to survive
cards.text: Soul Sacrifice is Marvelous AQL and Japan Studio's PlayStation Vita action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 7 March 2013. A prisoner awaiting sacrifice encounters Librom, a talking book containing the memories of a sorcerer's battles. Entering its stories lets the prisoner gain the experience needed to challenge Magusar, the captor waiting outside. Each mission becomes another remembered encounter with a monster, connecting repeated battles to the account inside the book. The bleak setting makes the power offered to the player feel dangerous before its cost is fully understood.

cards.heading: Every powerful action asks for something
cards.text: Offerings supply the magic used during a quest, turning objects into different attacks and defensive effects. Their limited use asks the player to choose an appropriate set before entering a battle and judge when to spend it. More extreme abilities draw on the character's body, making the idea of sacrifice visible in the powers themselves. The system gives a large attack a consequence beyond consuming an ordinary magic bar. A successful encounter therefore depends on preparing useful abilities and deciding how much of that preparation to commit.

cards.heading: Choose what happens after the fight
cards.text: Defeated beings can be saved or sacrificed, and those choices shape the character's development. The decision gives the aftermath of a battle its own place in the progression system rather than treating it as an automatic reward screen. Cooperative play lets several sorcerers confront the same threats, adding other people to the balance of risk and rescue. Keiji Inafune conceived the project, with Yasunori Mitsuda and Wataru Hokoyama composing its score. The expanded Soul Sacrifice Delta followed in 2014, adding another version of the book's brutal world.

main.title: StarCraft II: Heart of the Swarm
main.subtitle: Kerrigan reclaims the Swarm and evolves its armies
main.summary: The second part of Blizzard’s StarCraft II trilogy follows Sarah Kerrigan’s campaign against Arcturus Mengsk. Evolution missions and new Zerg units extend the strategy of Wings of Liberty.

cards.heading: Kerrigan returns in the second part of the trilogy
cards.text:
StarCraft II: Heart of the Swarm is an expansion pack to the military science fiction real-time strategy game StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty, and the second part of the StarCraft II trilogy developed by Blizzard Entertainment, with the final part being Legacy of the Void. The game was released on March 12, 2013.

The expansion includes additional units and multiplayer changes from Wings of Liberty, as well as a continuing campaign focusing on the Zerg race and following Sarah Kerrigan in her effort to regain control of the swarm and exact her revenge on the Terran Dominion's emperor, Arcturus Mengsk.

cards.heading: The Leviathan, Abathur and the evolution missions
cards.text: Heart of the Swarm features a single-player campaign with 20 missions (plus seven evolution missions which allow the player to upgrade units), and continues the story from Wings of Liberty. The player plays from the perspective of Sarah Kerrigan, recently returned to her human form by Jim Raynor. Similar to Wings of Liberty, the briefing room allows interactive exploration, this time on the Leviathan, an enormous Zerg breed which functions as a bioship. Kerrigan and her allies are located in the nerve center. She has a personal chamber for altering her abilities, and there is an evolution pit where she can upgrade her units and perform evolution missions with the evolution master Abathur.

cards.heading: Vipers and Swarm Hosts change Zerg tactics
cards.text: The Viper supports Zerg armies with abilities that reduce an enemy's range, pull a target closer or draw energy from a friendly structure. The Swarm Host burrows and produces waves of Locusts, allowing an army to maintain pressure without spending resources on each attacker. Locusts cannot attack air units, so other forces must cover that weakness.

main.title: God of War: Ascension
main.subtitle: Kratos breaks his oath to Ares
main.summary: God of War: Ascension is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3.

cards.heading: Kratos faces the Furies
cards.text: God of War: Ascension is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3. Released in March 2013, it is the seventh installment in the God of War series and the second chronologically. Loosely based on Greek mythology, it is set in ancient Greece with vengeance as its central motif. The player controls the protagonist, Kratos, the former servant of the God of War Ares, who tricked Kratos into killing his own wife and daughter. In response to this tragedy, Kratos renounced Ares, breaking his blood oath to the god. Kratos was, therefore, imprisoned and tortured by the three Furies, guardians of honor and enforcers of punishment. Helped by the oath keeper, Orkos, Kratos escapes his imprisonment and confronts the Furies, aiming to free himself of his bond to Ares.

cards.heading: Reworked combat and the first multiplayer mode
cards.text: Combat centres on the Blades of Chaos, with discarded weapons available through the World Weapons system. Four magical attacks, a power-enhancing ability, puzzles and platforming accompany the familiar combinations of attacks. Some encounters use quick-time prompts, while others let Kratos respond without an explicit button prompt. Ascension also introduces online competitive and cooperative multiplayer, the first such modes in the series.

cards.heading: Reception and award nominations
cards.text: Reviews praised the combat and large-scale spectacle, while finding the story less compelling than earlier entries. Multiplayer drew a mixed response: reviewers welcomed the adaptation of the fighting system but questioned its balance and depth. The game shipped more than three million copies and received nominations for writing and sound design.

main.title: Gears of War: Judgment
main.subtitle: A Military Trial Rewrites the Gears Campaign
main.summary: Gears of War: Judgment revisits the war through Kilo Squad and asks players to change the terms of an encounter.

cards.heading: Before the familiar trilogy
cards.text: Gears of War: Judgment follows Kilo Squad shortly after Emergence Day, before the events of the original trilogy. Damon Baird and Augustus Cole fight alongside Sofia Hendrick and Garron Paduk in Halvo Bay. Epic Games and People Can Fly released the Xbox 360 game in March 2013.

cards.heading: An encounter with extra conditions
cards.text: Mission Declassification adds optional conditions to campaign encounters. The Smart Spawn System varies enemy types, arrival times and positions, so returning to a familiar space can produce a different fight.

cards.heading: Attack and defence exchange sides
cards.text: OverRun pits five-player teams with distinct classes against one another. Teams alternate between COG and Locust, switching the weapons, abilities and responsibilities used to attack or defend.

cards.heading: People Can Fly takes the lead
cards.text: Development on Gears of War: Judgment began after the release of Gears of War 3 in September 2011. Epic Games brought in developer People Can Fly to lead the development, making this Epic and People Can Fly's second collaboration after Bulletstorm. PCF was previously developing a sequel to Bulletstorm before being assigned to work on Judgment.

main.title: Luigi’s Mansion: Dark Moon
main.subtitle: A fractured moon sends Luigi back into haunted mansions
main.summary: Next Level Games brings Luigi’s ghost-catching adventure to Nintendo 3DS. The Poltergust 5000, Strobulb and Dark-Light Device turn haunted rooms into puzzles during the Year of Luigi.

cards.heading: Luigi returns to Evershade Valley
cards.text: Luigi's Mansion: Dark Moon (known as Luigi's Mansion 2 in Japan, Australia and Europe) is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Next Level Games and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS. It is the second installment in the Luigi's Mansion series, following Luigi's Mansion (2001). The story follows Luigi as he explores Evershade Valley, capturing its corrupted ghostly inhabitants with help from Professor E. Gadd. In order to restore peace to Evershade Valley, Luigi must defeat the recently-escaped King Boo and restore the eponymous Dark Moon.

cards.heading: Stunning ghosts and uncovering hidden objects
cards.text: A charged Strobulb flash stuns a ghost so Luigi can catch it with the Poltergust 5000. The vacuum also carries objects, pulls switches, turns valves and launches items to solve room puzzles. The Dark-Light Device reveals invisible doors, furniture and hidden Boos. Coins improve the Poltergust, while each mansion contains gems and Boos to find.

cards.heading: Next Level Games and the Year of Luigi
cards.text: Next Level Games developed Dark Moon under Nintendo supervision, exploring the dual screens and depth display of 3DS. Its delay to 2013 made it part of Nintendo's Year of Luigi. Critics praised the haunted locations and new tools while questioning the mission structure and limited checkpoints. The game sold 6.44 million copies by December 2020, with later arcade and remastered adaptations extending its life.

main.title: Warframe
main.subtitle: The Tenno and Digital Extremes’ cooperative missions
main.summary: Warframe is a free-to-play action role-playing third-person shooter multiplayer online game developed and published by Digital Extremes.

cards.heading: Warframe reaches PC and other platforms
cards.text: Warframe is a free-to-play online action game developed and published by Digital Extremes. It first launched for Windows in March 2013 and reached PlayStation 4 later that year, followed by other platforms. Cooperative missions mix third-person shooting, close combat and parkour. Later updates added cross-platform play and shared account progress.

cards.heading: The Tenno, Warframes and missions
cards.text: In Warframe, a player controls a member of the Tenno, a caste of ancient warriors who have awoken from centuries of suspended animation far into Earth's future to find themselves at war with different factions in the Origin System. The Tenno use biomechanical combat units called Warframes, along with a variety of weapons and abilities, to complete missions. While many of the game's missions use procedurally generated levels, it also includes large open world areas similar to other massively multiplayer online games, as well as some story-specific missions with fixed level design. The game includes elements of shooting and melee games, parkour, and role-playing to allow players to advance their Tenno with improved gear. The game features both player versus environment and player versus player elements. It is supported by microtransactions, allowing players to purchase in-game items with money, while also offering the option to earn them at no cost through grinding.

cards.heading: From Dark Sector to a self-published game
cards.text:
The concept for Warframe originated in 2000 when Digital Extremes began work on a new game titled Dark Sector. At the time, the company had been successful in supporting other developers and publishers but wanted to develop its own game in-house. Dark Sector suffered several delays and was eventually released in 2008, incorporating some of the initial framework but differing significantly from the original plan. By 2012, in the wake of the success of free-to-play games, the developers took their earlier Dark Sector ideas and art assets and incorporated them into a new project, their self-published Warframe.

Initially, the growth of Warframe was slow, hindered by moderate critical reviews and low player counts. However, since its release, the game has experienced significant growth. It is one of Digital Extremes' most successful titles, reaching nearly 50 million registered players by 2019.

main.title: BioShock Infinite
main.subtitle: Booker and Elizabeth in the airborne city of Columbia
main.summary: BioShock Infinite is a first-person shooter video game developed by Irrational Games and published by 2K.

cards.heading: Booker and Elizabeth between Columbia factions
cards.text: BioShock Infinite is a first-person shooter video game developed by Irrational Games and published by 2K. The third installment of the BioShock series, Infinite was released worldwide for the PlayStation 3, Windows, Xbox 360, and OS X platforms in 2013. The game is set in the year 1912 and follows its protagonist, Booker DeWitt, who is sent to the airborne city Columbia to retrieve Elizabeth, a young woman held captive there. Booker and Elizabeth become involved in a class war between the nativist Founders that rule Columbia and the rebel Vox Populi, representing the city's underclass. Elizabeth possesses the ability to manipulate "Tears" in the space-time continuum, and Booker and Elizabeth discover she is central to Columbia's dark secrets. The player controls Booker DeWitt throughout the game, fighting enemies and scavenging supplies, while the computer-controlled Elizabeth provides assistance.

cards.heading: American history and the relationship between the protagonists
cards.text: After the 2007 release of BioShock, Irrational Games and creative director Ken Levine were initially uninterested in creating a sequel, but they later renegotiated with 2K to produce another BioShock game. Irrational based the game's setting on historical events at the turn of the 20th century, such as the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition, and based the story on the concept of American exceptionalism while also incorporating influences from more recent events at the time such as the 2011 Occupy movement. The relationship between Booker and Elizabeth became central to the story, with the team working to make Elizabeth feel like a real character rather than a computer-controlled sidekick.

cards.heading: Five years of development and Burial at Sea
cards.text: The game's development took five years and involved hundreds of employees at Irrational, in addition to support studios. The development process was troubled, with Levine's management style resulting in wasted work and missed deadlines. Outside help was brought in to make sure the game shipped. BioShock Infinite was supported post-launch with downloadable content, including the story expansion Burial at Sea, which links Infinite's story to that of the original BioShock game.

cards.heading: Critical reception and later editions
cards.text: BioShock Infinite received critical acclaim, with praise particularly directed at its story, setting, visual design, and art direction. It has sold more than 11 million copies worldwide. Infinite was re-released for the PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch as part of BioShock: The Collection.
